issue.title: referenced-by write-back reports a TypeError instead of the git failure: _pull_rebase_if_remote builds an undecoded bytes issue message
issue.description:
`_pull_rebase_if_remote` builds its failure detail from an undecoded `subprocess`
result, so a failing `git pull --rebase` produces a `bytes` issue message that later
crashes the string join in the drain path.

`sase.sdd.referenced_by_refresh._pull_rebase_if_remote` calls
`run_sdd_git(["remote", "get-url", "origin"], ...)` and
`run_sdd_git_write(["pull", "--rebase"], ...)` without `text=True`, and
`run_sdd_git` defaults to `text: bool = False` (`src/sase/sdd/_git.py:40`). When the
pull fails, `detail = result.stderr.strip() or result.stdout.strip() or "git pull
failed"` is therefore `bytes`, and it is stored verbatim as
`ReferencedByRefreshIssue.message`.

`sase.agents_sync.referenced_by_publication.drain_referenced_by_requests` then runs
`"; ".join(issue.message for issue in report.errors)` at line 64 and raises
`TypeError: sequence item 0: expected str instance, bytes found`.

Two consequences beyond the crash:

1. The real `git pull --rebase` failure is never reported. The caller
   (`sase.agents_sync.prompt_archive.publish._drain_referenced_by_after_prompt_publish`,
   line 318) catches every exception and reports only
   `referenced-by write-back failed: <TypeError text>`, so the operator sees a Python
   type error instead of the git error that actually stopped the write-back.
2. The outbox is never advanced. The `TypeError` is raised on line 64, *before*
   `update_referenced_by_requests(...)` on line 65, so the escaping exception skips
   both the acknowledge and the failure-recording paths. Those requests keep their
   old attempt count, never reach `quarantine_threshold`, and retry forever with the
   same undecoded failure.

Suggested fix: pass `text=True` to both `run_sdd_git` calls in
`_pull_rebase_if_remote` (or decode `detail` before constructing the issue). A
regression test should assert that a failing pull yields a `str` message and that
`drain_referenced_by_requests` records the failure on the outbox rather than raising.
Consider also hardening line 64 to coerce non-`str` messages, so a future undecoded
message degrades to a bad diagnostic instead of an escaping exception that strands
the outbox.

task_type_fields.impact:
## Impact

Hits every agent whose commit finalizer publishes a prompt archive while a sidecar
pull fails. The primary commit still lands, so no work is lost, but:

- the operator-facing warning names a Python `TypeError` instead of the git failure
  that caused it, which makes the condition effectively undiagnosable from the
  message alone;
- the referenced-by outbox requests are neither acknowledged nor failure-recorded, so
  they never increment attempts and never quarantine — they retry indefinitely and
  keep producing the same useless diagnostic on every subsequent publish.
task_type_fields.location: src/sase/sdd/referenced_by_refresh.py:_pull_rebase_if_remote (detail from run_sdd_git without text=True); crash site src/sase/agents_sync/referenced_by_publication.py:64
task_type_fields.repro:
## Reproduction

Observed live on 2026-08-28 on `sase` master at `bcd6813d2`, while resuming a paused
commit in the `research` sidecar:

```bash
sase stitch create --resume
# ⚠️ The primary commit succeeded, but prompt archive publication was deferred and
# will retry with agent publication: referenced-by write-back failed: sequence
# item 0: expected str instance, bytes found
```

The trigger is any failing `git pull --rebase` inside a sidecar that has an `origin`
remote, while a referenced-by outbox request is pending for that role.

Direct unit-level reproduction of the root cause:

```python
from sase.sdd.referenced_by_refresh import _pull_rebase_if_remote
# In a sidecar checkout with an origin remote and a pull that fails
# (e.g. diverged history with rebase disabled), the returned issue's
# .message is bytes, not str:
issue = _pull_rebase_if_remote(repo_root)
assert isinstance(issue.message, str)  # fails: it is bytes
```

Then `"; ".join(issue.message for issue in report.errors)` in
`referenced_by_publication.py:64` raises the `TypeError` above.

payload.description: Both are defects in sase.sdd callers of run_sdd_git (src/sase/sdd/_git.py:32); sase-u9 hits its unbounded per-ref subprocess loop, sase-va hits its text=False default leaving stderr as bytes
